cells.tense: Right now you are the one holding the direction, and you know how you chose it.
cells.ask: Ask the person you are growing what they want next, and follow that for one week instead of your plan for them.
cells.core: You're holding a direction that matters, and your grip is easy. What you defend, you defend as something you picked, not something you got cornered into. The care you've put into growing this has a steady hand on it — you can feel when to push and when to stand back, and the reading you get is usually right.\n\nWhat this balance is free to feed next is shared joy. Meaning passed back and forth, teaching that shifts as it goes, people belonging without having to match. So ask the person you are growing what they want next, and follow that for one week instead of your plan for them. What you hear will move the direction somewhere better than where you were going to take it alone.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the direction and still let it be changed by what you hear.
cells.verb: Holding a chosen direction against what pushes back
cells.place: Where something small is being tended toward its own growth

cells.tense: You will have defended this through the moment when it stopped needing defending at all.
cells.ask: Let one decision about what you tend go the way the other person wants it, and watch what happens over a week.
cells.core: You're defending something that isn't under attack yet. The next move gets planned before this one lands, and you carry a picture of how it has to go that nobody in the room agreed to. From your side it reads as protection. From theirs, it starts to feel like a plan they weren't let in on.\n\nThe care is not the problem. What's missing is the ease that lets you hold a direction and set it down anyway. So let one decision about what you tend go the way the other person wants it, and watch what happens over a week. You know how to hold a line. The practice here is letting one line be theirs.

cells.tense: You stopped putting your weight behind the direction, and the door you passed is well behind you.
cells.ask: Take the smallest next step for what you tend, today, where one other person can see you take it.
cells.core: You know what you care about, and you have stopped moving it forward. Where you once stood up for the direction, now there is upkeep — quiet, careful, and it can go on a long stretch without the thing getting any bigger. The pull is still there. The standing behind it is what thinned out.\n\nThe way back runs through the smaller, steadier work, not a big push. Take the smallest next step for what you tend, today, where one other person can see you take it. You don't have to feel moved first. The motion tends to come after the step rather than before it, and the step is small enough to take tired.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped moving the direction and called the upkeep enough.

cells.tense: You are already holding the direction steady while describing it as only what needed doing.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you are holding steady and why you picked it, in a sentence you would actually say.
cells.core: You are already the one holding this steady. You gather the scattered parts, you keep the small thing alive, and you file it under what needed doing. The pick is yours and it goes unnamed. Going well here would look like someone saying out loud what they are keeping and why, and letting the people around them hear the choice in it.\n\nThat gap costs you something. The work is real, and neither you nor anyone else is saying what it is. The way out is smaller than you'd think. Tell one person what you are holding steady and why you picked it, in a sentence you would actually say. Say it once, plainly, and let it stand without taking it back.
